newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-GANZ SENDS INTER INTO UEFA CUP SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GANZ SENDS INTER INTO UEFA CUP SEMIS.

text.p: Maurizio Ganz scored both goals on Tuesday as Inter Milan beat Anderlecht 2-1 on Tuesday to move into the UEFA Cup semifinals 3-2 on aggregate.

Ganz, who scored in the first-leg 1-1 draw in Belgium, took his competition total to five with two headers in the San Siro to end Anderlecht's hopes but it was a far from vintage performance from the Italians.

"The thing that mattered was to win," said Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson, whose team are looking at the UEFA Cup to redeem a season which has otherwise turned sour, with a place in the top two in the Italian league slipping away.
Anderlecht's hopes got off on the wrong foot on the eve of the match when first-choice goalkeeper Geert De Vlieger twisted his ankle getting off the team bus.
They also lost influential midfielder Danny Boffin after 18 minutes with a leg injury.
Stand-in goalkeeper Frederic Herpoel did a brave job but could do little to prevent the goals, both of which derived from poor marking.
Ganz got the first in the 12th minute with a close-range header from a cross by Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff.

His second after an hour was a more spectacular diving header when he connected with a cross from Argentine Javier Zanetti to keep Inter on course for a third UEFA Cup title in seven years. The club were champions in 1991 and 1994.

Anderlecht had equalised in the 33rd minute when Ghanaian striker Yaw Preko, who has not scored in the Belgian league since September, ended his goal drought by prodding in on the volley a cross from Swede Par Zetterberg.
Zetterberg, who was one of the most impressive players on the pitch, set up several chances which went begging.

Ganz, who had a second-minute goal disallowed for offside, had opportunities to complete a hat-trick before Hodgson pulled him off in the 76th minute to make way for Dutchman Aron Winter, who was sent packing to the stands at the weekend after a row with the boss.
The crowd gave Ganz a standing ovation while booing Hodgson's tactics.
"I think everyone understood the substitution," said Hodgson, at pains to rule out more talk of divisions at the club after recent newspaper stories.
"It had to be either Ganz or Djorkaeff as (Ivan) Zamorano was too important to us for free-kicks and penalties."
Chilean striker Zamorano had a poor game, missing several chances including a clear header when left unmarked in front of goal.
But Hodgson dismissed suggestions that Inter looked below par, saying: "It was a difficult match, difficult for Anderlecht above all."
Anderlecht's Dutch coach Johan Boskamp, who has already announced his departure at the end of the season, said De Vlieger's injury was a "silly way" to get hurt.
"We could have won. Inter had a lot of problems with how we played," he added.
